en: A first-class lever like a seesaw multiplies force when the fulcrum is placed closer to the heavy load.
A ramp reduces the effort needed to lift a heavy box by spreading the work over a longer distance.
Rough surfaces like sandpaper create more friction than smooth glass, causing a sliding object to stop much faster.
Earth's gravity constantly pulls objects toward its center, causing a dropped apple to fall straight down to the ground.
Opposite poles of two magnets attract, pulling the north pole of one directly toward the second magnet's south pole.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow through the wire and light up the bulb.
Light bends when passing from air into water, making a straight straw look broken inside a drinking glass.
Plucking a guitar string creates physical vibrations that travel through the air as sound waves to reach your ears.
Heat transfers through conduction when fast moving particles in a hot metal spoon collide with slower particles in your hand.
A stretched rubber band stores potential energy, which instantly transforms into kinetic energy the moment you release it.
A fixed pulley changes the direction of force, allowing you to pull a rope downward to lift a flag upward.
Running an electric current through a coiled wire wrapped around an iron nail temporarily turns the nail into a magnet.
